issues.description: Template StockIngredient exposes the quantity via retrieveQuantity(), while Stock and the specification/solution expect a getQuantity() method. This prevents students from compiling when Stock.java calls stockIngredient.getQuantity() and conflicts with the "add getters for all private fields" requirement.
issues.suggestedFix: In the template StockIngredient.java, rename retrieveQuantity() to getQuantity() (or add a public getQuantity() that returns quantity and optionally keep retrieveQuantity() as a delegating alias) so Stock.java and the required getters match the intended API.

issues.description: The problem statement requires SealSaloon.stock to be a final Stock instance and explicitly states it must be static, but the UML diagram shows it as an instance association (non-static) and the narrative also says it is initialized in the constructor. This contradiction can confuse students about whether stock should be per-instance or shared across all saloons.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the UML and text: either (a) update the UML to mark stock as {static} (and clarify it is initialized as a static final field), or (b) remove the requirement that stock is static and update solution accordingly. Prefer (a) to match the existing solution and method static requirements.

issues.description: StockIngredient's quantity getter is named retrieveQuantity() in the template but getQuantity() in the solution and implicitly expected by Stock/SealSaloon logic. This breaks conceptual mapping for the same 'quantity' property across artifacts and can cause students to implement against the wrong identifier.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename template method retrieveQuantity() to getQuantity() (or add a getQuantity() wrapper delegating to retrieveQuantity()) so the quantity property uses a consistent getter name across template, problem expectations, and solution.
